summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on experience debugging hardware/software integration failures across Jetson, STM32, and Arduino systems in Linux environments. Strong in Python and C++, with a computer-architecture foundation spanning CUDA kernel optimization, bare-metal firmware, and concurrent FreeRTOS task coordination. Comfortable building automation and benchmarking tooling to test, profile, and root-cause complex system-level issues.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID cursor commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; root-caused and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary — Robotics
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national competitions and multiple engineering sub-teams; designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE and implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 hardware/software integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, false-positive detections) to reach 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.
Built a vision-guided pick-and-place system over a three-layer distributed pipeline: Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller over a WebSocket fabric.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) for visual servoing and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over an I2C mux; implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across concurrent servo-control and sensing tasks.
Ran YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending interrupt-driven commands to an STM32 over UART with multi-servo PWM control and user override.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms (uncoalesced) and 77.5ms (CPU TorchScript) — ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.
Replaced TorchScript conv layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
